requirements.title: Segments are statement sequences before, between, or after image control statements on an image
requirements.definition: On each image, the sequence of statements before the first image control statement, between two image control statements, or after the last image control statement is a segment. The immediately preceding segment includes expression evaluation within the image control statement; if no image control statement executes before termination, the whole statement execution sequence is one segment.

requirements.title: Programs can establish segment ordering; otherwise cross-image segments are unordered and may overlap
requirements.definition: By image control statements or user-defined ordering, a program can ensure that one image segment precedes or succeeds a segment on another image. If the program does not ensure this, the segments are unordered; depending on relative execution speeds, some or all execution of the unordered segments may take place at the same time.

requirements.title: Unordered cross-image segments are restricted for ordinary variables, coarray subobjects, and effective arguments
requirements.source: 11.7.2 p3 otherwise bullets; J3/24-007 PDF p231.
requirements.definition: Except for the specified atomic, event, notify, and satisfied NOTIFY= cases, unordered segments shall not contain conflicting cross-image ordinary variable actions, shall not inquire about or change specified coarray subobject properties across images unless ordered, and shall not access an effective argument on another image while the defining noncoarray dummy argument procedure invocation is in execution unless the other segment precedes the first or succeeds the last procedure segment.

requirements.title: Actions on a variable are ordered when their containing segments are ordered
requirements.definition: If an action regarding X occurs in segment Pi on image P, segment Pi precedes segment Qj on image Q, and an action regarding X occurs in segment Qj, then the action regarding X in Pi precedes the action regarding X in Qj.

review_rationale: Independent fresh-context source review against the pinned J3/24-007 PDF: doc/source_audits/batch_123.json. The reviewer re-read the original sections (PDF p230-235), re-derived unit hashes rather than accepting the author receipt, and independently recomputed the census. Two blocking findings were closed by correction commit cf1fff9 and re-verified by the same reviewer: C117SR-001 (11.7.4 image-set bounds collapsed the positive, upper-bound and no-repeated-values obligations into single facets, contradicting the packet's own compound sweep) and C117SR-002 (11.7.2 p3 and 11.7.5 p4 were dispositioned permission although each carries normative shall restrictions; both are now split so obligations and latitude are disposed separately). Source accounting only: no fixture was bound, authored_facets is unchanged at 1839, and no executable oracle or runtime credit is claimed. All of 11.7 is image execution control and this suite has no multi-image capability, so synchronization, segment ordering, scheduling and failure-dependent behaviour carry no executable oracle.
